title: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP) Header
reproductionSteps: 1. Execute native curl command: curl.exe -I -s -S https://www.amankumarx1.xyz/
3. Verify that neither 'Content-Security-Policy' nor 'Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only' is present.
observedEvidence: Headers include Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy, but lack Content-Security-Policy.
expectedBehavior: A Content-Security-Policy header restricting script execution, style sources, and frame ancestors should be returned on all HTML documents.
securityImpact: Without a CSP, the application lacks defense-in-depth against client-side script injection and malicious inline script execution in the event of an XSS vulnerability.
remediation: Add a Content-Security-Policy header in vercel.json headers section: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self';

title: Server Banner Information Disclosure (Vercel)
expectedBehavior: Generic or suppressed Server header to prevent reconnaissance of underlying hosting platform.
securityImpact: Reveals the edge infrastructure provider (Vercel) and edge node geographic point of presence (bom1 - Mumbai).
remediation: While standard for Vercel, consider stripping or obscuring custom platform headers via edge middleware if strict banner suppression is required by corporate policy.

title: Overly Permissive Wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin on HTML Document
expectedBehavior: CORS headers should be scoped specifically to public static assets or API endpoints, rather than top-level HTML document responses.
securityImpact: Permits arbitrary third-party web origins to read response bodies via XMLHttpRequest / fetch. While currently benign on this static portfolio, it establishes an insecure precedent if private dynamic content is later introduced.
remediation: Remove the wildcard CORS header from HTML page responses or restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to trusted origins.
